title: AI-driven cyberattacks hit 16 financial firms, expose 100,000 records
key_facts: Number of financial firms hit by suspected AI-agent-driven cyberattacks rose to 16, from seven first reported, regulators said on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
About 100,000 records with personal data, including resident registration numbers, were exposed; the tally could rise.
Affected firms include banks Shinhan, KB Kookmin, BNK Busan and Hana, plus savings banks, credit finance firms, payment providers and crypto businesses.
No evidence so far that account or card numbers were compromised.
Regulators are checking whether one hacking group is behind the attacks.
130 of 555 inspected financial firms (23.4%) had security deficiencies, such as missing patches and no 24-hour monitoring.
The Financial Services Commission plans broader reforms, including making CEOs and boards more accountable.
quote_evidence: The number of financial firms affected by suspected artificial intelligence (AI) agent-driven cyberattacks has risen to 16, more than double the seven initially reported, financial regulators said Wednesday.
About 100,000 records containing personal information, including resident registration numbers, were exposed.
why_it_matters_hint: Attacks on Korean finance have more than doubled in reach and exposed ID numbers of ordinary customers.
event_date: Attacks since the start of Oct 2026; regulator update 14 Oct 2026
notes: The article does not name the tools or models used; the AI-agent link is described as suspected. Earlier pool item (11 Oct) named ARTEX AI and Claude agents; not repeated here because today's article does not.
